extracted.intended_audience: U.S. government officials and the public (1861); historians and researchers
extracted.subtask_description: A collection of Abraham Lincoln's official letters, orders, proclamations, and memoranda from March–May 1861 relating to appointments, military measures, proclamations of militia and blockade, suspension of habeas corpus, and diplomatic instructions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Ambassadorial appointment considerations
rubrics_metrics.description: Select appointees based on eminent fitness for the place, advice/suggestion of Secretary, and pressure/representation from their States; be mindful of regional clustering but accept responsibility if necessary.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Text: 'These gentlemen all have my highest esteem... Mr. Adams I take because you suggested him, coupled with his eminent fitness for the place. Mr. Marsh and Mr. Burlingame I take because of the intense pressure of their respective States, and their fitness also. The objection to this card is that locally they are so huddled up... I have considered this, and will not shrink from the responsibility.'

rubrics_metrics.name: Publication of military despatches (Fort Sumter inquiry)
rubrics_metrics.description: Do not publish despatches of a military commander to the War Department if, upon examination, publication would be 'inexpedient' or incompatible with the public interest.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Text: On receiving Senate resolution requesting Anderson's despatches, Lincoln: 'On examination of the correspondence thus called for, I have, with the highest respect for the Senate, come to the conclusion that at the present moment the publication of it would be inexpedient.'

rubrics_metrics.name: Preparation and readiness for naval expedition
rubrics_metrics.description: An expedition by sea should be got ready to sail on a set date with specified steamers, crew, stores for one month, designated numbers of men ready at particular ports, supplies for twelve months in portable shape, and conditionally engaged tugs/steamer.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Inclosure lists: 'Steamers Pocahontas at Norfolk, Paunee at Washington, Harriet Lane at New York... Three hundred men to be kept ready... Two hundred men to be ready to leave Governor's Island... Supplies for twelve months for one hundred men to be put in portable shape... A large steamer and three tugs conditionally engaged.' Also directs cooperation between Secretary of War and Secretary of the Navy.

rubrics_metrics.name: Secrecy and command assumptions in naval operations
rubrics_metrics.description: An officer assuming command of any available naval steamer for a special mission shall proceed with least possible delay, prevent enemy expeditions at all cost or risk, and keep the order, its object, and destination confidential until reaching the destination harbor.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Text of order to Lt. D. D. Porter: 'You will proceed ... and with the least possible delay, assuming command of any naval steamer available, proceed to Pensacola Harbor, and at any cost or risk prevent any expedition from the mainland reaching Fort Pickens or Santa Rosa Island... This order, its object, and your destination will be communicated to no person whatever until you reach the harbor of Pensacola.'

rubrics_metrics.name: Cooperation for relief expeditions (Fort Sumter)
rubrics_metrics.description: All officers of the army and navy to whom an order is exhibited shall aid by every means in their power an expedition under a named commander, supplying men and material and cooperating as he may desire.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Order dated April 1: 'All officers of the army and navy to whom this order may be exhibited will aid by every means in their power the expedition under the command of Colonel Harvey Brown, supplying him with men and material, and co-operating with him as he may desire.'

rubrics_metrics.name: Temporary reassignment/detachment for special purposes
rubrics_metrics.description: When circumstances require placing an officer in command for a special purpose, the officer to be detached should be informed that the detachment is for special purpose only and not a reflection on his efficiency; convey confidence and intent to provide better command later.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Confidential order to Captain Samuel Mercer: explains detachment for special purpose, expressly states it does not reflect on his efficiency and promises better command later.

rubrics_metrics.name: Conditions for calling forth militia (Proclamation calling for 75,000)
rubrics_metrics.description: The President may call forth the militia when laws are opposed and their execution obstructed in States by combinations too powerful to be suppressed by ordinary judicial means or marshals; call is for suppression of combinations and to cause laws to be executed, with details communicated through War Department.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Proclamation (April 15): 'Whereas the laws of the United States have been ... opposed, and the execution thereof obstructed, in the States ... by combinations too powerful to be suppressed by the ordinary course of judicial proceedings, or by the powers vested in the marshals by law: Now, therefore ... do hereby call forth the militia ... to suppress said combinations, and to cause the laws to be duly executed.' Also: command to 'disperse and retire peacefully' within twenty days and convening Congress in extra session.

rubrics_metrics.name: Establishment and rules of blockade (April 19 & April 27 proclamations)
rubrics_metrics.description: When insurrection prevents effective execution of laws and threatens commerce (e.g., letters of marque), the President may set on foot a blockade of ports; competent force posted to prevent entrance/exit, commanders to warn vessels attempting to violate blockade and capture repeat offenders; molestation of U.S. vessels punishable (may be treated as piracy).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Proclamation (April 19): cites insurrection in named States and threats to commerce; prescribes warning procedure and capture for repeat attempts; declares persons molesting a U.S. vessel 'amenable to the laws of the United States for the prevention and punishment of piracy.' April 27 extends blockade to additional ports due to seizure of public property and obstruction of officers.

rubrics_metrics.name: Policy statement on holding federal property and use of force
rubrics_metrics.description: The President's policy: use power to hold, occupy, and possess property and places belonging to the Government, and to collect duties and imposts; beyond what is necessary for these objects there will be no invasion or use of force against the people; but, if forts are assaulted or seized, he will repossess like places and repel force by force as necessary.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Reply to Virginia Convention (April 13): Reaffirms inaugural: 'The power confided to me will be used to hold, occupy, and possess the property and places belonging to the Government... but beyond what is necessary for these objects, there will be no invasion, no using of force against or among the people anywhere.' Also states possible withdrawal of mails and repossession of seized posts.

rubrics_metrics.name: Centralized adoption and energetic prosecution of policy
rubrics_metrics.description: Once a general line of policy is adopted, it must be energetically prosecuted and directed incessantly; either the President must lead and be active in it or devolve it on a Cabinet member, with debates ending and uniform adherence.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: From Seward memorandum and Lincoln's reply: Seward urged changing the question to union/disunion and the need for energetic prosecution; Lincoln responded that when a general line is adopted he must do it while still expecting Cabinet advice on points arising.

rubrics_metrics.name: Localized suspension of the writ of habeas corpus
rubrics_metrics.description: Military commanders are authorized to suspend the writ of habeas corpus at or near specific points on military lines when resistance there renders suspension necessary for public safety.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Order (April 17): 'If at any point on or in the vicinity of any military line ... between the City of Philadelphia and the city of Washington you find resistance which renders it necessary to suspend the writ of habeas corpus for the public safety, you personally, or through the officer in command at the point at which resistance occurs, are authorized to suspend that writ.'

rubrics_metrics.name: Enrollment of loyal citizens into military service (St. Louis)
rubrics_metrics.description: The President may direct enrollment of loyal citizens up to a specified number for maintaining authority and protection of peaceful inhabitants; while enrolled they are governed by Rules and Articles of War and special regulations; martial law may be proclaimed if necessary; arms and stores not needed should be removed to safe deposit.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: War Dept. letter (April 30): authorizes Captain Lyon to 'enroll in the military service of the United States the loyal citizens of Saint Louis and vicinity, not exceeding ... ten thousand' and permits proclamation of martial law; 'The arms and other military stores ... not needed ... must be removed to Springfield, or some other safe place.'

rubrics_metrics.name: Call for volunteers and increases in Regular Army and Navy
rubrics_metrics.description: When exigencies demand, the President may call specified numbers of volunteers for fixed terms (e.g., 42,034 volunteers for three years unless sooner discharged), increase the Regular Army by specified regiments and numbers, and direct enlistment of seamen in addition to present force; details to be provided by Departments and submitted to Congress.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Proclamation (May 3): spells out numbers and terms: 'call into the service ... 42,034 volunteers to serve for the period of three years... increase the Regular Army ... making altogether a maximum aggregate increase of 22,714 officers and enlisted men... enlistment for ... 18,000 seamen.'

rubrics_metrics.name: Suspension of the writ of habeas corpus in specified territories (Florida)
rubrics_metrics.description: When insurrection exists and loyal citizens and officers are endangered in a State or territory, commanders on the coast may be directed to permit no officer to exercise inconsistent authority, to suspend the writ of habeas corpus where necessary, and to remove dangerous or suspected persons from the vicinity of federal fortresses.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Proclamation (May 10): 'I ... direct the commander of the forces of the United States on the Florida coast to permit no person to exercise any office or authority upon the islands ... which may be inconsistent with the laws and Constitution of the United States, authorizing him at the same time, if he shall find it necessary, to suspend there the writ of habeas corpus, and to remove from the vicinity of the United States fortresses all dangerous or suspected persons.'

rubrics_metrics.name: Diplomatic conduct toward foreign recognition and unofficial intercourse
rubrics_metrics.description: Ministers are to avoid any intercourse, official or unofficial, with agents/commissioners of insurgent entities where such intercourse may be construed as recognition; base no proceedings on parliamentary debates beyond seeking explanations; transmit and confine communications properly to State Department.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Corrections to despatch (May 21): 'You will base no proceedings on parliamentary debates further than to seek explanations... You will in any event desist from all intercourse whatever, unofficial as well as official, with the British Government, so long as it shall continue intercourse of either kind with the domestic enemies of this country.' Also emphasizes clear record and delivery to Secretary of State.
